prerequisites: Basic concepts of classical mechanics (motion, forces, Newton's laws)
Fundamentals of particle kinematics and dynamics
General notions of energy and work

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling students to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts on the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving engineering problems.
Structure discourse to facilitate understanding of the objectives, actions, and/or results of one's own work.
Solve complex problems autonomously within the discipline.
Draw conclusions from practical or experimental work and research carried out autonomously.

syllabus_topics: Centers of gravity of a two-dimensional body
First moments of areas and lines
Centers of gravity of a three-dimensional body
Determination of moment of inertia by integration
Radius of gyration of an area
Moments of inertia of composite areas
Components of the moment of a force
UNIT 6: Kinematics of the Rigid Body
Kinematic magnitudes of a rigid body
Linear velocity and acceleration at a point of the rigid body
Angular velocity and acceleration of rotation about an axis
General equations of velocity and acceleration
UNIT 7: Dynamics of the Rigid Body
Angular momentum of a rigid body
Fundamental equation of rotation of a rigid body around a fixed axis and a principal axis of inertia
Conservation of angular momentum of a rigid body. Applications
Kinetic energy of translation and rotation of a rigid body

assessment_methods.method: Written test, first partial (open-response and objective parts)
Written test, second partial (open-response and objective parts)
Oral exam/defense (continuous assessment: classroom participation in autonomous complex problem-solving)
Classroom and/or computer practical test (evaluation using instrumentation or specific resources)
Integrated Project presentation and oral defense

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.3·I1 + 0.3·I2 + 0.05·I3 + 0.1·I4 + 0.15·I5 + 0.1·I6, where each instrument is scored out of 10. A minimum of 4 points (out of 10) in tests I1 and I2 is required to average with other grades. The minimum overall grade to pass the course is 5 out of 10. For the second call, students can either retake one or both partial tests while maintaining continuous assessment, or retake the entire course, waiving continuous assessment and the Integrated Project.
